newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-Jan 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** The Economic Times newspaper said on Thursday that the government estimates India's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 6.7 percent in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31 over the preceding year.
The daily newspaper said the government's Economic
Survey for 1996/97 was set to estimate GDP growth at 6.7 percent, "which is a considerable improvement on the earlier expectation that it was slowing down to about six percent".
Last week the government said GDP grew by 7.1 percent in
1995/96 and by 7.2 percent in 1994/95.

** Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is due to hold a board meeting on Thursday to discuss, among other issues, a new takeover code, a SEBI official told Reuters on Wednesday.
The meeting -- scheduled for Thursday morning in Bombay
-- will also discuss a stock lending scheme, an amendment in the country's share depository act and a report on short sales, the official said. She did not give any further details.
** The Indian government on Wednesday played down expectations that a large package of measures to spur financial markets would be announced this week, saying its efforts were broadly focused.
A government spokesman was asked if New Delhi, as widely
expected in the financial capital Bombay, would announce a large package of measures this week to shore up the capital markets where stocks and bonds are traded.
"The capital market is an important segment. The
government effort is to move on a very broad front so the economy picks up in all sectors, not just the capital market," he told Reuters by telephone.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.865/875 against the dollar on Thursday compared with the previous close of 35.855/865, dealers said.
Some dealers expect a spurt in dollar demand on Thursday
putting mild pressure on the rupee.
** A wave of profit-taking at higher levels dragged down Indian stocks on Monday, with most blue chips ending with sharp losses, traders said.
** The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index (BSE) fell over two percent to end at 3,525.97 off 3,645.35. Total turnover at the exchange amounted to 9.83 billion rupees.
** The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index was down 4.60 points, or 0.45 percent, to 1,017.20
** The Delhi index fell 2.3 percent to 749.87
** The Calcutta index lost 1.42 percent to 453.14
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
